conventions.convention: CAT(1) requires geodesics only for distances strictly below π and comparison only for triangles of perimeter strictly below 2π. Comparison inequalities quantify over side occurrences, including repeated vertices and degenerate triangles.

Angular distances are truncated at π; auxiliary infinity between intrinsic components is never an ordinary metric value. Short comparison tests agree with untruncated intrinsic tests. Empty links satisfy CAT(1) vacuously and have one-point cones.
Local CAT means an induced-metric closed ball is CAT. Local geodesics have one fixed constant speed, including speed zero; minimizing geodesics satisfy the same distance equality globally.

The Alexandrov upper angle is the infimum over ε>0 of suprema of Euclidean comparison angles with both positive radial parameters at most ε. No ordinary limit or monotonicity is built into its definition.

All loops are normalized proportionally to arclength. Short means length strictly below 2π. Short-loop homotopies are continuous in uniform convergence plus length convergence and include both endpoints in the shortness requirement.

Fix n≥3, a uniform radius 0<l<π/2 and 0<h<l. Tuple indices are modulo n; P_h(n) uses mesh≤h, while midpoint definability uses mesh<l. The basin is defined by iterated lengths tending to zero, independently of shrinkability. Degenerate pairs have their common point as midpoint.
The positive uniform decrement applies only to basin tuples with length in (0,2π). Its function depends on n and length, independently of X and mesh, and tends to zero at both endpoints.

The compact short-circle theorem assumes AC. Injectivity radius is the supremum of radii below which all pairs have unique minimizing geodesics; failure of CAT(1) produces an embedded circle of twice that radius.
Products use the square-sum metric and componentwise geodesics. Product polygon energies add, but squared polygon lengths generally do not.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A compact geodesic locally CAT(1) metric space X is CAT(1) iff it contains no isometrically embedded circle of length <2π. If X is not CAT(1), it contains such a circle of length 2 injrad(X)<2π, with injrad(X)>0. If 0<R≤π and all pairs at distance <R have unique geodesics, every triangle of perimeter <2R satisfies all-pair spherical comparison.

For a metric space L, its cosine-metric Euclidean cone C(L) is CAT(0) iff (L,min{π,d}) is CAT(1), including the empty-link convention. For a connected locally finite isometric polyhedral gluing with finitely many shapes, local CAT(0) at a relative-interior point of F is equivalent to CAT(1) of its truncated normal face link; local CAT(0) everywhere is equivalent to CAT(1) of every vertex link.

A closed rectifiable curve of length 2r<2π in a CAT(1) space lies in the radius-r/2 ball about the midpoint of endpoints splitting it into equal-length arcs. The stated inward quadrilateral configurations admit a positive continuous separation deficit δ(η,μ). Under AC, for a basin tuple and a finite midpoint cellulation with nondegenerate comparison faces and final-row length <2l, the comparison disk is CAT(1). If additionally 0<L(x)=2r<2π and every edge ξ_i≥r/n, some midpoint edge satisfies ζ_k≤(ξ_k+ξ_{k+1})/2−δ((π−r)/2,min{r/(2n),(π−r)/2}).

Assume AC. For compact locally CAT(1) X and fixed l,n≥3,0<h<l, there is a continuous positive λ_n:(0,2π)→(0,∞), depending only on n and length, such that E(fx)≤E(x)−λ_n(L(x)) for every basin tuple with 0<L(x)<2π. On every band 0<a<b<2π a uniform bounded number of iterations takes basin tuples of length ≤b below a. The basin is open in P_h(n) and closed in its length-<2π piece.

Assume AC. Let X be compact, geodesic and locally CAT(1), and let m be the infimum of its embedded-circle lengths, with m=∞ if none exist. Every short loop γ with L(γ)<m is shrinkable; equivalently every loop of length <min{m,2π} is shrinkable. If m<2π, m is attained by a short nonshrinkable embedded circle and is the minimum nonshrinkable length. CAT(1), m≥2π, shrinkability of every short loop, and absence of embedded circles of length <2π are equivalent.

In a complete locally CAT(0) metric space, each constant-speed local geodesic c:[0,1]→X has a uniform ε>0 such that endpoints within ε admit exactly one local geodesic c′ with convex separation from c. Its separation is everywhere <ε, its length is at most L(c) plus the two endpoint displacements, and it depends continuously on those endpoints in the sup metric.

For connected complete locally CAT(0) length X and x₀∈X, the space of constant-speed local geodesics from x₀ is sup-metric complete and contractible. Its induced length metric is complete and has the same topology; endpoint evaluation is a local isometry and a surjective universal covering. The general complete-local-isometry covering criterion additionally requires continuous local endpoint dependence of geodesics in the connected locally uniquely geodesic target.

A connected complete simply connected locally CAT(0) length metric space is CAT(0). Endpoint evaluation from each local-geodesic path space is a covering and a homeomorphism; each pair has exactly one local geodesic, which minimizes. Its continuous geodesic contraction satisfies d(H_t(x),H_t(y))≤t d(x,y).

alerts.finding: Facts [F4], items/thm-cg-large-metric-flag-short-loop-radial-contradiction.md:68, says “every loop of length below the infimum m of the lengths of isometrically embedded circles is shrinkable”. The opened supplier lem-cg-bowditch-quantitative-short-loop-control, Statement (iii), instead says “Every short loop” with length <m, equivalently length <min{m,2π}. The general fact as quoted drops this domain restriction: a compact interval has m=∞ and rectifiable backtracking loops of length ≥2π, whereas shrinkability is defined only for short loops. The consumer's actual contradiction argument invokes m<2π, but [F4] states a broader supplier proposition.

seams_checked.note: The consuming definitions and cone/link theorem preserve angular truncation, normal face versus point links, empty cones, square-sum products, and the locally finite finite-shapes chart hypotheses. Connectedness is supplied for the polyhedral theorem; the external chart itself works in the point's connected component.

The opened downstream citation clauses preserve both cone-equivalence directions, the strict CAT(1) tests, local-geodesic length ≤π, and the compact-circle theorem's AC, compactness and geodesicity assumptions. Compact-circle applications explicitly use untruncated geodesic components.

The radial-insertion and nerve uses preserve normalized uniform-plus-length short homotopies and the compact geodesic AC hypotheses. However, thm-cg-large-metric-flag-short-loop-radial-contradiction [F4] omits “short” from the below-m shrinkability proposition. See the owning-group alert; its actual proof invocation has m<2π.
